What is in the catalogue?

Public evidence records can include observed measures, reproducible derived measures, source records, historical evidence, programme or reform observations, and explicit unknown or conflicting states. Each item keeps a persistent reference and its links to the relevant questions and pages.

Source directory and verification

Sources that support the evidence now published are listed separately from references kept for verification or context, so that a link is never mistaken for analytical use or an observed result.

Every source here can be cited and opened where it was originally published. Each card says whether the source’s reuse terms have been assessed; where they have not, this resource offers no copy of the source for download or republication.

This resource links to original sources and quotes them briefly. Reuse terms have not been assessed for most sources, and a public link is not permission to republish a source's content; check the original publisher's terms before reusing any material from it.

Curated reports and references (28)

Reports, methods and implementation references

The directory includes a deliberately small set of curated primary Yemen reports and international methods and implementation references alongside the full register of links to original sources. They help interpret payment infrastructure, financial-inclusion measurement, cash-transfer digitisation, MSME finance and the current reform and economic context. They are reference resources, not substitute evidence for Yemen, and this resource links to the original publisher rather than republishing a source file unless redistribution permission is explicitly established.

Research and analysis on Yemen’s financial sector

Yemen Financial Sector Diagnostics (2024)

World Bank · Research or policy paper · 2024Reference SRC-WB-FSD-2024-001

Does not establish: A diagnostic is not a current administrative census or regulator statement. Institution-level and survey results retain their own dates, universes, methods and limitations.

Open original source ↗ (opens in a new tab)
About this source

A major analytical reference covering CBY-Aden, banking, money transfer and exchange services, access to finance, and the 2022 Yemen Enterprise Survey annex; useful for sector structure, historical context and source triangulation.

Reuse terms: not assessed

Evidence records using this source (8)

  • Finance severity within a specific denominator
  • Three observed survey waves, not an annual series

  • Finance is not the only constraint surveyed formal firms report, 2022
  • Loan sources in 18 valid responses from surveyed formal firms, 2022
  • Finance obstacle severity among surveyed formal firms, excluding those that said they needed no loan, 2022
  • Formal firms in the 2022 survey: accounts were common, bank finance for working capital was not

Beyond Financial Soundness: Rebuilding the Supervisory Framework for Microfinance Banks in Yemen (2026)

Al-Amal Microfinance Bank (published on FinDev Gateway) · Research or policy paper · September 2026Reference SRC-AMB-MFB-SUPERVISION-2026

Does not establish: A proposal published by a microfinance bank: it is not a statement by the regulator or an independent assessment. It treats the Central Bank of Yemen as a single supervisor, without distinguishing the one in Aden from the one in Sana'a, and it does not show how microfinance banks are supervised in practice or whether any institution is operating, and it provides no sector figures used by this resource.

Open original source ↗ (opens in a new tab)
About this source

A policy brief by Mohammed Al-Lai and Dhekra Al-Gabri, published by Al-Amal Microfinance Bank, on how Yemen’s microfinance banks are supervised. It argues that supervision should assess social and developmental performance alongside financial soundness, which makes it a useful starting point for regulators and providers asking how licensing and supervision relate to inclusion outcomes.

Reuse terms: not assessed

Rules, decisions and official lists (38)

These are the regulatory documents held in this evidence base, not a complete register of Yemen's financial regulation. All but one were issued or posted by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden; its undated pages on credit-risk information cite older instructions, the earliest from 1991. The one instrument issued in Sana'a, a circular of the Central Bank of Yemen – Sana'a on paying out incoming external transfers, is held in the copy a news site republished. This group holds no law; the one law the evidence base holds, on the Bank Deposit Insurance Institution, is listed below with the other sources.

Open original source ↗ (opens in a new tab)
About this source

The circular of the Central Bank of Yemen in Sana'a on how banks and exchange companies acting as main agents for external remittance services pay out incoming transfers: transfers in Saudi riyals are paid in Saudi riyals; individual transfers in US dollars are paid in their Saudi-riyal equivalent at the dollar rate its Foreign Exchange Dealing Unit approves, and those in other foreign currencies at the international selling rate against the Saudi riyal on the day the transfer was issued; it applies from 14 March 2024.

What it means

A value copied from here still needs its context

A number without its unit, population or base, period, geography and source can become a different claim when reused. When you copy or cite a figure, take its evidence record reference with it so that its meaning travels with the value.

What availability does not mean
What this does not establish

What availability does not mean

A public record is not automatically nationally representative, current, comparable to another record or free for unrestricted redistribution. Availability tells you that the record can be displayed; it does not tell you that the underlying data may be redistributed, and it does not remove its methodological limits.

System context

Reuse terms belong to the original publisher

Some sources permit public display but not redistribution of the underlying table; others permit source metadata while the values themselves remain restricted. Reuse terms have not yet been assessed for most sources in this library, so most source records do not state them. The original publisher’s terms apply and should be checked before any redistribution. Including a source here does not mean CauseWay endorses its analysis or conclusions.

What we still do not know

What you may not find

A missing record may mean the evidence has not been found, is not comparable, is rights-restricted, is unsafe to publish at the requested resolution, or genuinely does not exist in the current evidence base. The catalogue must not turn any of those states into zero.

Verify the evidence

Open the evidence record before reuse

From any catalogue result, open the evidence record to check the definition, population or calculation base, period, geography, source authority, derivation, evidence type and how current it is, reuse terms where recorded, limitations and correction history.
